newsitem.title: POLAND: FORECAST - Polish CPI seen down, trade gap widening.
newsitem.headline: FORECAST - Polish CPI seen down, trade gap widening.

text.p: Polish inflation is seen falling below 15 percent in May while rising industrial output should help push unemployment to new lows, said Tadeusz Chroscicki, chief analyst at the government's Centre for Strategic Studies (CSS).
In his macroeconomic forecast, submitted monthly to Reuters, Chroscicki said fast rising imports will, however, drive Poland's current account and trade deficits to new highs.
"The negative relation between the growth rate of exports and imports...is worsening and causing the rapid growth of Poland's foreign trade deficit," Chroscicki said.

He said that even if export revenues continued to grow by 10 percent compared with last year, import payments might be 30 percent higher resulting in an ever widening trade gap and adversely affecting foreign currency reserves.
The report said inflation might be only marginally above 15 percent next month and drop below that level in May putting this year's inflation target of 13 percent within reach.

Official forex reserves are hard currencies held by the central bank while net reserves are the total amount of foreign exchange in the banking system. Indicators marked (R) are results, rest are forecasts.
